explain.say: Every time you move something, you use a push or a pull. Opening a lunchbox, kicking a ball, zipping a coat! A push or a pull is called a force. Look at the board. Let's sort some everyday actions.

explain.say: Look at this ball. See the arrow? Your kick is a push, and it makes the ball roll away. A gentle kick makes it roll slowly; a big kick makes it zoom! What happens if you kick it harder?
Now a tug of war: both teams pull with the same strength, the arrows are equal, so nobody moves! Well done! Challenge: count how many pushes and pulls you do before breakfast tomorrow.

forces.label: Team B pulls
forces.ask: Why does nobody move in tug of war?

faq.a: A force is a push or a pull. Forces can make things start moving, stop, speed up, slow down, change direction or change shape.

faq.q: Is opening a door a push or a pull?
faq.a: It can be either! If the door opens away from you, you push it. If it opens towards you, you pull it. Many doors have a sign saying which.
asks: Is opening a drawer a pull?

faq.q: Why does nobody move in tug of war?
faq.a: When both teams pull equally hard in opposite directions, the forces balance, so the rope stays still. The stronger team makes it move their way.

faq.q: What happens if you push harder?
faq.a: A bigger push makes things speed up more. A gentle kick rolls a ball slowly; a hard kick sends it flying.
asks: Does a bigger force make things go faster?

faq.q: Can a force change the shape of something?
faq.a: Yes. Squeezing play dough, stretching a rubber band or squashing a sponge are forces changing an object's shape.

facts: A force is a push or a pull, measured in newtons.
When forces on an object are balanced, its motion does not change.

quiz.say: You open a drawer towards you. Is that a push or a pull?

quiz.why: Moving something towards you is a pull.

wrong.0: A push moves things away from you.
wrong.2: Opening a drawer needs a force, so it is a pull.

quiz.say: In tug of war, both teams pull equally hard. What happens?
quiz.show: Equal pulls in tug of war…
quiz.why: Equal forces in opposite directions balance, so nothing moves.

wrong.1: Equal pulls do not have to snap a strong rope.
wrong.2: Balanced forces keep everyone in place, not falling.
